patch.value: Refresh verified stat cache after materialization without trusting concurrent bytes

Cubic review exposed a tension in the initial materialization cache: recording a post-write stat can pair the expected object id with bytes concurrently replaced by another process, while omitting metadata makes status re-read restored or switched files until a later stage. Design a safe cache warm-up that verifies content and updates metadata only after the timestamp window, without turning a read-only status into a racy index overwrite.

After restore or switch, an aged unchanged file reaches metadata-only status without explicit add; a concurrent write at every materialization and refresh boundary is detected; index updates use compare-and-swap or locking so status cannot overwrite a concurrent stage; installed-CLI strace acceptance proves content reads stop; full coverage remains 100/100/100
Materialized files safely warm the stat cache and later status calls avoid content reads.
Correctness-first materialization currently omits stat metadata because an unverified post-write stat can hide a concurrent edit.

value.author: codex
value.text: Cubic reiterated the post-materialization performance gap on the latest head. It remains intentionally open: the current PR removes unsafe metadata to prevent a concurrent false-clean; this item owns the correctness-safe verified warm-up with index CAS or locking.
